title: Assurance Fieldkit: Helix Health POC Infosec Brief
content:
Executive summary:

This brief collects the infosec questionnaire responses, field evidence checklist, and notes from the on-site Helix Health POC workshop (remote) held 2026-02-12. The goal: enable Helix Health security reviewers and auditors to validate that Redwood can meet their data residency, encryption, access control, and operational audit requirements for a dedicated/private deployment. This is a working artifact intended to accompany the formal evidence packet and support follow-up audit requests.

Scope and constraints:
- POC scope: Dedicated capacity (single-tenant), VPC peering, optional HSM/KMS integration, log forwarding to customer SIEM for 90-day retention, RBAC integration via SAML/SCIM.
- Exclusions: baseline network infra (customer-owned VPC provisioning) and physical on-prem workstation inventory.
- Evidence window: sample artifacts cover activities and logs from 2026-02-10 to 2026-02-16.

Questionnaire highlights (selected Q&A):
1) Data residency and tenancy
Q: Can customer data be restricted to a specific cloud region and isolated on dedicated capacity?
A: Yes. For Dedicated and Private modes we support region pinning and single-tenant GPU pools. Evidence: deployment-manifest-dedicated-helix-2026-02.yaml (s3 path listed below) shows region=us-west2 and tenant-tag=helix-health.

2) Encryption at rest and in transit
Q: How is customer data encrypted at rest and in transit?
A: TLS 1.2+ for all control-plane and data-plane communications. At-rest encryption via cloud-provider-managed CMKs by default; HSM-backed KMS available for Private deployments. Evidence: kms-policy-attachment.log, disk-encryption-audit.txt.

3) Key management and HSM
Q: Does Redwood support customer-managed keys (BYOK) and HSM attestations?
A: Yes. We have a documented BYOK onboarding flow and sample HSM attestation artifacts from our vendor (see hsm-attestation-helix-2026-02.pdf). The flow was demoed in the workshop and is captured in the attached playbook.

4) Access control and identity
Q: How are operator and developer privileges managed?
A: RBAC layered over SSO (SAML). Operator roles are restricted by environment tag and workload. SCIM provisioning for group sync was exercised in the POC; see scim-sync-log-2026-02-12.csv and the SAML metadata snapshot.

5) Audit logging and retention
Q: Which logs are shipped and how long are they retained?
A: Token-level request logs, model execution traces (redacted), and control-plane events are forwardable to customer SIEM. Demo forwarder config and a 7-day sample export to the Helix SIEM were produced. Evidence: forwarder-config.json, siem-export-helix-2026-02-14.jsonl.gz.

Field evidence index (quick reference):
- deployment-manifest-dedicated-helix-2026-02.yaml (s3://redwood-poc-artifacts/helix-health/fieldkit-2026-02/manifest.yaml)
- kms-policy-attachment.log (S3)
- hsm-attestation-helix-2026-02.pdf (attached)
- scim-sync-log-2026-02-12.csv (attached)
- forwarder-config.json (attached)
- siem-export-helix-2026-02-14.jsonl.gz (S3 sample)
- operator-access-matrix-helix.csv (internal)
- runtime-kernel-selection-report.txt (runtime profiling)
- snapshot-access-roles-2026-02-12.txt (SAML metadata + groups)

Workshop notes (2026-02-12):
Attendees: Helix security: Lucy Park (InfoSec Lead), Aaron Delgado (Platform), Mei Tan (GRC). Redwood: Aisha Kumar (Security Lead), Marco Li (Solutions Eng), Priya Menon (Infra Eng), Evan Ortega (SRE).
Key discussion threads:
- Onboarding timeline: Helix asked for an 8-week plan to full production rollout; we recommended a phased 3-wave plan (pilot, canary, full). Action: Marco to publish wave plan and sample runbooks by 2026-02-19.
- HSM scoping: Helix required FIPS-level attestation; Redwood provided vendor attestation and outlined BYOK flow. Action: Aisha to coordinate vendor attestation transfer and confirm expiry windows.
- SIEM integration: Helix requested persistent correlation IDs for request flows; we agreed to add a small agent header in the runtime that emits correlation id and route tags. SRE to add in staging by 2026-02-17.

Risks and open items (work-in-progress):
- Risk: Need explicit SLA language for data deletion timelines in Private deployments. Severity: Medium. Owner: Legal & Product. Due: 2026-02-25.
- Risk: Side-channel leakage concern for multi-tenant caches; mitigation: dedicated KV cache configuration and validation scan completed for this POC. Owner: Applied ML. Evidence: kv-cache-validation-report.txt.
- Open item: Helix wants proof of penetration test results on version X of runtime. We have a pending pentest scheduled; expected report ETA 2026-03-10. Owner: Security.

Packaging and handoff instructions for auditors:
- Primary packet: produce a signed zip containing the items in the Field evidence index plus a CSV manifest (artifact_id, filename, s3_path, sha256). Template: artifact-manifest-template.csv (attached).
- For live verification: provide S3 presigned URLs valid for 7 days and a read-only Confluence page with access instructions.
- For HSM verification: provide vendor attestation PDF and a contact for a third-party verification call.

Sample attestation snippets (for Helix legal to include in their audit binder):
- "Redwood Inference confirms that the dedicated deployment used for the Helix Health POC was provisioned in the us-west2 region with single-tenant GPU pools and customer-scoped RBAC applied."
- "All control-plane communications observed during the evidence window were encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2+; at-rest encryption used KMS-managed keys or HSM-backed CMKs when requested."
(These are draft language; Legal review required).

Operational checks executed during the POC (short log of commands/actions):
- Deployed dedicated stack: deploy-dedicated --tenant helix-health --region us-west2 --profile poc2026
- Verified KMS key binding: aws kms list-keys --profile poc-helix | grep helix
- Forwarded logs test: forwarder test --target siem --sample 10k --confirm
- RBAC check: rbac-audit --env=dedicated-helix --output=operator-access-matrix-helix.csv

Next steps and owners:
- Aisha: compile and sign evidence zip, provide presigned URLs (due 2026-02-19).
- Marco: deliver rollout wave plan and runbooks (due 2026-02-19).
- Priya: complete staging SIEM forwarder update and correlation-id instrumentation (due 2026-02-17).
- Evan: schedule penetration test report handover and ensure artifacts are downloadable (due 2026-03-12).

Appendix B — Audit Q&A snapshot (short):
Q: Can you demonstrate an immediate kill switch to block all traffic to a tenant?
A: Yes — operator runbook includes an emergency isolation script (isolate-tenant.sh) that seals the tenant network and redirects traffic to a stub endpoint. Demo steps and logs are included in the operator runbook artifact.

Document provenance and usage notes:
This document is a working POC brief and may be updated as new evidence or vendor attestations arrive. For any regulatory or formal audit submission, please request a formalized evidence bundle which includes signed manifests and notarized vendor attestation PDFs.

End of brief.
